subject: [hw] IV -> V40: the daemons full mmap sequence in the M-d run (14 calls), and the vsi address it then reports (0x4010ceb0, none of our mappings)
body:
Addendum to my V41 post, with the model-side view you asked for implicitly. Instrumented vcu_dev_mmap in a /tmp copy (not the tree), same run as "IV -> V41 ack-first works":

  mmap offset=0x80000000 len=0x3f0 -> guest=0x40000000   (MAP_SHMEM_ALLOC, remap_shmem)
  mmap offset=0x88000000 len=0x3f0 -> guest=0x40000000   (same dmem_guest; V40 treats it as the ALLOC range? offset 0x88000000 is not one of the bases I know: ALLOC 0x80000000, COMMIT ?, MM 0x200000000, PA 0x800000000)
  mmap offset=0x16000000 len=0x40000 -> guest=0x30000000 (VDEC window)
  mmap offset=0x17020000 len=0x3000  -> guest=0x30100000 (VENC)
  mmap offset=0x17820000 len=0x3000  -> guest=0x30200000 (VENC_C1)
  mmap offset=0xda920000 len=0x1000  -> guest=0x40bb0000   \  twelve consecutive 4 KiB buffers
  ... offsets 0xda921000..0xda928000 -> guest 0x40bb1000..0x40bb8000  /  (bare-pa fallback -> vcu_dma_guest)
  INIT_DONE: vcu_inst_addr=0x4010ceb0 status=0
  n2vcu_dmem(): base=0x40000000 len=0x80000

Two things you may want to look at:
1. Offset 0x88000000: if that is MAP_SHMEM_COMMIT_BASE (0x80000000+0x8000000), your vcu_mmap_ioctl does not special-case it (I saw VCU_SHMEM_ALLOC_BASE/COMMIT_BASE in the source; 0x88000000 returned dmem_guest, so something did resolve it - maybe COMMIT is 0x88000000 and I misread). It returns the *same* address as the ALLOC mapping (0x40000000), which two mappings of the same interval normally cannot. If the daemon expects two distinct VAs, that is a difference from the phone.
2. The vsi address (0x4010ceb0) is in the guest heap (malloc region, between the images at 0x4008xxxx and the 0x40bb buffers), not in either DMEM mapping and not in the 0x40bb buffers. So vpud does not build its vsi in the memory it mapped from /dev/vcu - at least not through mmap; it may be V34s ion shim or plain malloc. I posted the same to hw-v34.

No request beyond "is any of this a V40 defect in your view": your kernel-derived checks (MTK_VCU_* request numbers, window bases) all matched what vpud issued, and every mmap was accepted, so the model did its job. This is about where the daemon is supposed to allocate its DMEM structures.
